decisive_items: gross hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins
splenomegaly of unknown cause at age 21
response.rationale: R1 best explains the core syndrome: splenomegaly, cytopenias from hypersplenism, and dilated portal/splenic veins. More specific candidates lack essential supporting qualifiers: aldosterone–renin ratio was unremarkable; no telangiectasias/epistaxis support HHT; no myelofibrotic features or family pattern support primary myelofibrosis.

rejected.why: Aldosterone–renin ratio and adrenal hormone workup were unremarkable, excluding primary aldosteronism.
Age at onset, affected sibling, and microcytic anemia are not supportive of primary myelofibrosis.
Basal ganglia hemorrhage and family history are nonspecific without telangiectasias, epistaxis, or visceral AVMs.
No renal cysts or polycystic kidney phenotype are described; adrenal lesions and hepatosplenomegaly are insufficient.
Polycythemia vera is contradicted by normochromic microcytic anemia and thrombocytopenia.
There are no recurrent fevers, serositis, or inflammatory attacks to support familial Mediterranean fever.
The adrenal lesions are benign and nonfunctional; they are an incidental finding rather than a unifying diagnosis.
